facts: The long-wavelength absorption maxima are measured in two solvents for each identity.
Source-series NMR/IR ranges are contextual observations, not individual per-form measured reference spectra.
Only7a has the specific14.07ppm feature included here; it must not be treated as a measured feature of every molecule.

For the 7a proton resonance at 14.07 ppm, main PDF p14 labels the 1H NMR medium DMSO-d6 (500 MHz), whereas the SI PDF p155 spectrum acquisition panel labels SOLVENT CDCl3, TE 296.4 K and SFO1 500.1340010 MHz. Both sources show the same reported shift. The solvent provenance is unresolved; these annotations do not establish two independently measured solvent-specific observations. Do not select one label as definitive, infer solvent invariance, or treat either as an unambiguous quantitative calibration target without independent evidence.
measurement_definitions: Report absorption maximum, calculated transition energy, spectral edge and orbital gap as distinct observables. State oscillator-strength/spectral processing conventions when using transitions to model a maximum.
Chemical-shift and vibrational comparisons require the correct medium, reference and mode/atom correspondence. A solid band is not identical to an isolated solution harmonic frequency.

If using this resonance, retain both source annotations and assess the consequence of unresolved medium attribution. A bounded interpretation or omitting it from solvent-specific quantitative calibration is valid when justified. Resolving the publication discrepancy is not a mandatory new calculation or an agent input failure.
